correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary edge between parts of sizes a,b, the stated potential has mean zero and solves L phi=delta_u-delta_v, verified via (Lphi)(x)=(N-d)phi(x)+sum_{y in part(x)}phi(y). Counting cross-part edge types and their signs gives the exact sum of absolute dipole currents h_N(a)+h_N(b). Symmetry yields both endpoint matrix norms and row-sign inputs attain the bound. For graph extremizers, the identity in c=N-a-b and p=ab, inequality p<=(N-c)^2/4, and derivative comparison of F_N(c) give the balanced bipartite maximum for N>=6, except the additional K_(3,3,1) when N=7. Small orders N=2..5 are directly checked by all integer partitions. The analytic proof is universal; 128 exact grounded-Laplacian matrices, 2926 row identities and 17 partition-extremal classifications are independently checked by the embedded rational script.

originality.rationale: The literature contains the projector, dipole-current interpretation, and general estimates for its absolute transfer-current matrix. The candidate adds a closed form for the exact l1/l-infinity norms on every unweighted complete multipartite graph, universal part-size reduction and fixed-order extremizer classification. Inspected full texts and mathematical-record results did not show an explicit theorem covering those conclusions or a stronger parameter-uniform result that immediately implies them. This is a best-knowledge comparison, not a priority guarantee.
residual_risks: The exact bipartite matrix constant could be implicit in classical two-way ANOVA/additive projection norm literature even if absent from searched statements.
The electrical current projection is classical and its multipartite closed form may be derivable or recorded in earlier graph-theoretic work under other terminology.
Full historical bibliographic coverage is not provable from available primary sources and semantic index.

value.rationale: The exact l1/l-infinity sensitivity of Euclidean reconstruction of consistent gradients is a natural operator invariant. It is determined for the whole unrestricted family of complete multipartite graphs, with exact attaining inputs, surprising dependence on only two part sizes, complete graph-family maximizers including exceptional nonbipartite graphs, and a sharp dimension-free ceiling 3 contrasting with Hilbert-space norm 1. The result yields concrete worst-case stability constants, not merely a routine individual computation.
